purpose: Quantify algorithmic pseudo-detection instability across fixed R seeds under exactly the archived native observations, without refitting occupancy or treating seeds as ecological replicates.

design.seed_roster: ALL consecutive integers 1..256 inclusive, no replacement, filtering, or post-result retry

cohorts.q1: exclude kis-banyato, vadasz-turjan; 27 wetland sites / 351 native rows
cohorts.q2: ci == intervention; 13 wetland sites / 188 native rows

design.original_r_preprocessing: X0=1; season=1; reps=20; call pinned survreps once separately within each cohort after set.seed(seed)
design.raw_source_unit: CSV row; no assumption that rows or surv group keys are independent physical traps
design.target: per-site species recorded positivity, not latent occupancy or a causal effect
metrics: lost raw-positive site×species pairs per cohort per seed
number of repeated selections and distinct source rows per cohort
number of pseudo-detection disagreements on the same 13 native-positive Q2 sites between Q1 and Q2 at the same seed
frequency with which each native-positive site×species pair is lost across seeds, compared with exact probability from n native site rows and k positive rows
overall means, medians, ranges and 5%-95% seed quantiles, descriptive Monte Carlo SE, not field uncertainty
design.fixed_regressions: seed=123 reproduces Q1 3 lost, 287 unique raw rows, Q2 6 lost, 153 unique raw rows, and seven cross-cohort disagreements using previous authenticated source mapping
design.stop: No historical installed R package certification; no mainline EOG-WF fourth endpoint, occupancy likelihood, ecological A/B/M causality, or seed-based scientific replication.
